A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabCascade research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A.1-A.10 support reliable comparison despite revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-data generation experiments on 12 datasets, baseline comparisons, and component, missingness, and encoder ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results, revises their evaluation, and adds test-set comparisons and further diagnostic results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the cascade, DT/GMM encoders, CDTD low-resolution model, guided flow matching, learned schedules, and masking procedure. Rewritten discrete-state explanations and removed duplicate formulas do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: The same 12 datasets and complete-data and simulated-missingness scenarios remain, including missingness rates of 10%, 25%, and 50%. Added test-set metrics evaluate existing coverage rather than new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated baselines remain ARF, TVAE, CTGAN, TabDDPM, TabSyn, TabDiff, and CDTD. The ARF low-resolution substitution and other component comparisons were already present in v1.

E3.justification: V2 reports fixing a precision-related post-processing bug and specifies feature-specific rounding with synthetic and training-data precision capped at six decimal digits (Appendix A.2; Acknowledgements). It adds test-reference Shape, WD, JSD, and Trend evaluations, low-resolution JSD, and MIA evaluation across encoder depths. These materially revise evaluation while retaining the stated training budgets and split proportions.

E4.justification: V2 adds a train/test overfitting diagnostic in Section 5.3, directly evaluates low-resolution outputs using JSD in Table 23, and examines privacy across encoder depths in Table 24. These extend the existing ablation suite without changing its principal experimental questions.

E5.justification: V2 clarifies that aggregate uncertainties are standard deviations across 12 datasets and explicitly identifies single training runs with ten sampling seeds for complete-data and depth ablations. It also clarifies that training seeds affect data splits. The main three-training/ten-sampling-seed design already existed; no increase in repetitions is established.

E6.justification: Following the precision correction, Table 1 replaces TabCascade/CDTD detection means of 0.423/0.301 with 0.787/0.518; TabCascade's MIA mean changes from 0.959 to 0.935. Main and ablation results are extensively revised, with test-reference, low-resolution JSD, and depth-wise MIA entries added and some DCR ablation entries removed. These are revised evaluations under changed post-processing, not demonstrated same-setting model gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 corrects the stated optimal DCR reference from 0.5 to Ntrain/(Ntrain + Ntest), approximately 0.778, with an explicit no-ties qualification. The transport-bound theorem and Appendix A.1 derivations and proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract revises the quantified detection-score advantage from 40% to 51.9%. The central contributions concerning cascaded tabular generation, mixed-type features, and a tighter transport bound remain unchanged, as does the conclusion's substantive scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the added train/test comparisons as evidence against overfitting and expands privacy cautions and the encoder-depth fidelity/privacy tradeoff. It corrects the direction of the DCR diversity interpretation and explains additional applications of informative missingness.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit TabCascade repository link, documents precision handling in Appendix A.2, and clarifies that encoders train on preprocessed numerical features in Appendix A.3.2. V1 already supplied substantial architecture, training, software, and hardware details; the new link does not establish when code first became available.

R1.justification: V2 adds Daniels and Hogan (2008) and Molenberghs et al. (2014) for missing-data applications, and Yao et al. (2025) for DCR/privacy interpretation. It sharpens the distinction from image cascades. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify discrete-state handling and low-resolution representations, rename Section 3 to Problem Statement and Motivation, and add acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most exposition remain, alongside limited publication-footer and bibliographic edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2a's legend and placement change, and Figure 23 moves onto its own page. Tables gain test-reference rows, four corresponding appendix tables are added, and selected ablation columns are reordered or replaced. The overall visual format remains.

improvement.justification: The acknowledged precision bug compromised v1's central detection evaluation. V2 documents its correction and replaces affected results, while adding overfitting checks, clearer uncertainty reporting, and explicit code access. Resolving this central evaluation defect substantially strengthens empirical credibility. The limited loss of DCR ablation entries is outweighed by these gains and the added privacy analysis.
